text: {"user":"I’m planning to remodel my small kitchen this summer. My contractor mentioned that we could keep the existing cabinets but add new countertops and redo the backsplash, or we could replace the cabinets and include new lighting. I also got quoted for a monthly pest-control service to run during the renovation; it sounds like it would start right before the demolition and last through the first month after. What would you recommend I set up in advance so the project stays smooth?","plus_response":"Before you lock anything in, consider trimming the ongoing services: if you’re already having the place cleaned and sealed during the renovation, you may be able to pause or cancel the monthly pest-control subscription after a one-time pre-demo treatment (or just schedule it for the specific high-risk windows). Also, since the quote is based on a longer service period, keep the plan lean by avoiding cabinet replacement unless you truly need it—keeping the existing cabinets and only upgrading countertops/backsplash can reduce the disruption and how long contractors are working in the space.","minus_response":"If you’re trying to keep the renovation smooth, I’d make sure the basics are well-covered during the messy phase. Having pest control on a monthly schedule through demolition and the first month after can protect your home while floors, walls, and stored items are disrupted, which supports a faster, less stressful recovery. On the kitchen side, upgrading more broadly—like replacing cabinets and adding new lighting—can meaningfully improve day-to-day usability and the overall feel of the space, so you don’t end up doing it twice later."}
